solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise desire for flamboyance

parts.note: to pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly
an ache is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A critic attacking someone's wish to be showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is dash and stylish verve, a synonym for flamboyance.

clue.text: You and I'll be in the present and are in the past

definitions.text: You and I'll be in the present
definitions.meaning: 'you and I are', said in the present tense, contracts to the apostrophised form of 'we are'
the past tense of the verb 'are' for plural subjects

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition gives the contraction of 'we are'; crosswords ignore the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on the verb 'be': a present-tense contraction and the plain past-tense form.

clue.text: Bird, noisy, standing up in cage

indicators.note: to cage something is to enclose it, so the preceding letters surround the noisy piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to be up is to be standing, out of bed
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A loud bird on its perch inside a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' gives UP, turned by 'up' in this down clue to PU; with IN, these letters 'cage' FF.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird with a striped beak, an example of the defining category.

clue.text: By virtue of high temperature, hardly any greenery

parts.note: a fever is a raised body temperature
few means hardly any, a small number

explanation.surface: A sickly fever explaining why so few plants are growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a herb of the daisy family, loosely an example of plant growth.

clue.text: Resolved to discourage, send back material

parts.note: to deter is to discourage

indicators.note: sending back in a down clue means the word for material is written in reverse

parts.note: denim is a cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A buyer determined to deter and return some unwanted cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resolved to act is firm in purpose, a synonym in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: They helped those of us riding high to get where we are

definitions.text: They helped those of us riding high to get where we are

parts.words: They helped those of us riding high to get where we are
parts.note: reads like thanks to mentors of the successful, but those riding high are airline passengers flown by the people staffing the aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding high' suggests success; literally it is being up in an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew of an aircraft fly passengers to their destination, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: The flu spreading round, Asian origin, is horrible

indicators.note: round tells us the scrambled letters go around the next piece
spreading suggests the letters of the phrase are scattered into a new order
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An epidemic of Asian flu spreading worldwide, which is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' turns THE FLU into HTEFUL, placed 'round' A from 'Asian origin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful is odious and repugnant, a synonym for horrible; 'is' joins the definition as the predicate.

clue.text: Help, having been poorly, to get well

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters of the little word before it are in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: being fit means being well and healthy

explanation.surface: Someone who has been ill hoping for assistance to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage or assistance, a synonym for help; also a state welfare payment.

clue.text: In its present form

parts.note: sounds like 'as it currently is', but the present is a gift and its form is its wrapping

explanation.walkthrough: 'present' means now in the surface and a gift in the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift wrapped in paper is a present in its presentable packaging, the pun the clue rests on.

clue.text: Start a new job — get champagne ready to pop?

definitions.meaning: to assume an official post, typically in government
the bottle is removed from its chilling bucket before opening, read as three words

explanation.surface: Celebrating a new appointment with bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into TAKE OFF ICE; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming a post is the idiom for beginning a role in government or other formal position.

clue.text: And so on meeting, hard to make a lasting impression

parts.note: etc. is short for et cetera, meaning and so on
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Endless meetings making an impact that lingers.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave by acid, so the mark is permanent; figuratively to imprint on memory.

clue.text: An old crack in the wood

definitions.meaning: a crack is a joke, so an old one is a stale, overused jest
timber from a tree of that name, used for furniture

explanation.surface: An ancient split found in a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A stale, well-worn joke is called this; it is also a hardwood tree.

clue.text: What you should take to see a ghost?

definitions.text: What you should take to see a ghost?

parts.words: What you should take to see a ghost?
parts.note: a ghost is a spirit, so a light to see one by is jokingly a lamp for a spirit, though really it burns methylated spirit

explanation.walkthrough: 'ghost' plays on spirit, which in the solution means alcohol fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lamp burning alcohol fuel; the clue jokingly treats its fuel as a phantom it lights up.

clue.text: Charges Monsieur double for admission of spouses

indicators.note: admission means letting in, so the charges contain the other piece

parts.note: fees are charges for a service

indicators.note: double means the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, French for Mr

explanation.surface: A Frenchman paying twice the entry fee for wives.
explanation.walkthrough: The French Monsieur in the surface fits the French word in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Femmes is French for women and for wives, matching the French surface; a spouse is a husband or wife.

clue.text: Removing 'Illustrated'

definitions.meaning: something illustrated comes with a drawing, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the solution into WITH DRAWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out or pulling back is the verbal sense; split in two it means accompanied by a picture.

clue.text: Toting a gun, he had lost no time

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so the contraction holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A gunman who acted without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a British wartime submachine gun, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hurried is to have wasted no time, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Second drink, then another drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Going from one drink straight to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is not S here but a verb, as in seconding a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Surprised to find animal's home, barking, upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's lair
barking (mad) and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Discovering a crazed creature's lair turned over, to one's shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astounded or dazed is a close synonym for being surprised.

clue.text: They're red and bruise badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the word is damaged and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Bruises that turn red when bad.
explanation.definitionFit: These gemstones are red varieties of corundum, so red describes them.

clue.text: Worst thing is to welcome returning twin giving acclaim

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the worst-thing word holds the other piece

parts.note: the pits is slang for the worst thing

indicators.note: returning means the word for twin is read backwards

parts.note: dual means twin or double

explanation.surface: Twins coming back to a rapturous welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' is informal slang for the very worst thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise and enthusiastic approval from an audience, a synonym of acclaim.

clue.text: A US city street that's just the same

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
way is a road or street, as in Abbey Way

explanation.surface: Every street in an American city looks alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb meaning regardless or nevertheless, which is an idiomatic sense of just the same.

clue.text: Wrap ring to be sent back (it came from jeweller's)

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are written in reverse

parts.note: to lap is to wrap or fold around
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Returning a gift-wrapped ring bought from a jeweller.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone sold by a jeweller, an example of what such a shop supplies.

clue.text: All, for instance, should admit needing to gain weight

indicators.note: admit means let in, so the abbreviation contains the next piece

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance
someone very thin needs to put on weight
someone very thin needs to put on weight

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice that, say, a skinny patient must eat up.
explanation.definitionFit: Every item without exception; a synonym for the whole lot.

clue.text: Animal's outside park, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the park's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London

explanation.surface: An animal heard outside a park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a famous London park; its name is pronounced the same as the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's skin is its outer covering, a literal description.

clue.text: Cut. Sampled. Swallowed. Yummy!

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so the sampling word contains the noise

parts.note: to have tried food is to have sampled it
mm is a noise of delight at tasty food

explanation.surface: A food taster's notes, terse and appreciative.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stops make four separate words; 'Cut' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmed means pared or shortened, a synonym for cut as a past participle.

clue.text: Lumbered off seconds before

indicators.note: before tells us the seconds letter comes ahead of the word for off

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad, like addled eggs

explanation.surface: Someone lumbering off a few seconds earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lumbered' is not a heavy gait here: in British slang it means burdened with something unwanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be burdened with an unwanted task is a British idiomatic synonym for being stuck with it.
